elements.label: Figure 8.1: Addressing the social protection coverage gap
elements.description:
Three-panel conceptual diagram (y-axis: Level of protection; x-axis: Income or consumption in each panel). Source noted as Packard et al. (2019).

Panel A: 'Stylized state of social protection in developing country'. Blue block at lower left labeled 'Risk-pooling instruments for preventing poverty are tightly rationed, excluding many poor and vulnerable people'. Orange band in the middle-right labeled 'Social insurance combines actuarial and equity objectives with distortive and rationing effects'. Teal wedge at upper right labeled 'Market insurance is scant, expensive, and/or ineffective'.

Panel B: 'Policy to fill the current gaps in protection'. Blue block labeled 'Eliminate exclusion'. Arrow labeled 'Expand beyond narrow poverty-targeting'. Orange band labeled 'Shift equity elements to financing from broader-based (general revenues financed)'. Upper-right teal wedge labeled 'Ensure social insurance is actuarially fair' and 'Encourage more supply and demand of voluntary insurance'.

Panel C: 'Comprehensive insurance assistance'. Blue block at lower left narrowing to the right, with yellow band above it and orange and teal layers expanding to the right. Labels: 'Raise the realtve importance of voluntary to mandtory insturments through nudging' (arrow to teal area) and 'Taper-away assistance and subsidies from the top of the distribution, through tax systems' (with a red circle marking the transition point where the layers meet).

Pattern: moves from narrow coverage with a gap in the middle (A) to filled middle-income coverage (B) to a comprehensive layered system spanning the full income distribution with taper-away subsidies (C).
